summary: Adam Hardy is an architecture, history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (c. 1972–1975), later serving as Professor at De Montfort University (c. 1993–2005) and Cardiff University (c. 2005), and directing PRASADA.

Adam Pearcey works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, while also studying under numerous traditional Tibetan teachers, including the 14th Dalai Lama.

Adam Yuet Chau is a sinologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at Stanford University in 2001 after undergraduate studies at Williams College. He later joined the University of Cambridge, serving as Professor of the Anthropology of China.
Adele Schlombs is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She held a long-term post at the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln from around 1991 to 2021.

Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at the Universities of Erlangen-Nuremberg, Bonn (Magister and Dr. phil.), and Marburg (Habilitation), later serving as a Privatdozentin at Marburg and visiting professor at Vienna (c. 2005–2006).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who completed her doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She held professorial appointments at the University of Münster (from 1971; chair and director 1988–2000) and the University of Munich (1978, 1980).

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, PIMS, and Harvard University (PhD c. 2000–2007). She served as Assistant Professor at Chicago (2007) and Professor of Older Art History at Basel (2020).
Adeu Rinpoche was a Tibetan Buddhist figure and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche, and later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère worked in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Résident de France at Kratié in the French Protectorate of Cambodia and co-founded the Société Ethnologique de Paris, where he served as vice-president.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist educated at the University of Mumbai (BA, D.Litt.) and Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute. He taught at Rajaram College (1930–1962), Shivaji University (1962–1971), and founded the Jaina Chair at the University of Mysore (1971).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, and others, earning a PhD at Berlin (1826–1829). He was Professor of Sanskrit at Breslau (1833–1847; Rektor 1862–1863) and a librarian at Wrocław University Library.

Adolf Holtzmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Othmar Frank, Johann Andreas Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf at universities including Halle, Munich, and Berlin. He served as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at Heidelberg University (1852–1870).

Adolf Kaegi was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Zurich, Tübingen, and Leipzig under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He spent his career at the University of Zurich, serving as Ordinarius from 1893 to 1914.

Adolf Kiessling studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (c. 1856–1858). Over his academic career, he held posts at the University of Basel (c. 1869–1877), the University of Greifswald (c. 1877–1889), and the University of Göttingen.

Adolf Kirchhoff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh at Berlin (1842–1846). He taught at the Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and served as ordentlicher Professor at the University of Berlin from 1865.
Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University (c. 1871–1877) and under August Leskien (c. 1879). He held an academic post at Uppsala University from around 1877 to 1919.

Adolphe Regnier was an Indologist, linguist, and historian who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He taught eloquence at the Collège de France (1838) and German at the École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), later serving as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

Adriaan Scharpé was an Indologist who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda (c. 1932–1937). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978) and professor at Ghent University (c. 1958–1983).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and sinology. He earned a master's at the University of Auckland and a PhD at Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, later teaching at the European School of Culture and Theology before joining the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (2019).

Adrián Muñoz works in Indology and religious studies. He has served as Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and as a lecturer in South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).
